channel.title: Updated · Biology
channel.description: Life sciences: discoveries, medicine and biotech

item.title: FDA approves durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin around surgery for bladder cancer patients who cannot take cisplatin
item.description: The FDA approved an immunotherapy plus antibody-drug conjugate given before and after bladder removal for patients who cannot or will not take cisplatin, after a 695-patient trial showed longer event-free and overall survival. (FDA, The ASCO Post)

item.title: US measles deaths climb as the CDC's tally reaches six and states report ten, with cases above 5,400
item.description: The CDC now counts six US measles deaths in 2026 while state health departments report ten, cases have reached 5,412, and a regional health body is weighing whether the US has lost measles-elimination status. (CIDRAP, PolitiFact)

item.title: China approves Lilly's orforglipron, the first GLP-1 weight-loss pill cleared there
item.description: China's drug regulator approved Eli Lilly's orforglipron tablets for adults with obesity, or overweight plus a related condition, making it the first oral GLP-1 drug for weight management in the country. (Pharmaceutical Technology, Plataforma Media)

item.title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
item.description: In a non-randomized Dutch study of 231 young adults in refractory cardiac arrest, helicopter teams starting ECMO on scene saw 40% survive to discharge versus 20% with conventional care. item.title: An LHX2-DACH1 regulatory innovation drives basal progenitor expansion in the primate neocortex
item.description: A small DNA switch that controls the gene DACH1, with a feature shared among primates, helps the developing cortex make more of a special stem cell abundant in primate brains, in organoids and mice. (Pei-Shan Hou, Ching-Yu Chuang, Feng-Lan Chiu et al. · National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University; Academia Sinica; Kyoto University)

item.title: A multi-tissue atlas of genetic regulatory effects in sheep
item.description: SheepGTEx maps how DNA variants control gene activity across 51 sheep tissues and cell types, and ancient DNA shows breeding favored variants acting in just one or a few tissues, such as skin. (Mian Gong, Ziyang Zhuang, Xiangrong Sun et al. · Aarhus University)

item.title: The American Cancer Society now recommends regular PSA screening for prostate cancer, every two years from age 50
item.description: The American Cancer Society's new guideline recommends a PSA blood test every two years for average-risk men aged 50 to 69, and yearly from 45 for Black men and men with strong family history. (American Cancer Society, The New York Times)

item.title: FDA approves pimicotinib, a once-daily pill, for joint tumors that are hard to remove surgically
item.description: The FDA approved EMD Serono's pimicotinib for symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor after a placebo-controlled trial in which 56% of treated patients responded, against 3.2% on placebo. (FDA, HMP Global Oncology)

item.title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma
item.description: In a phase 3 trial of 1,137 people with resected high-risk melanoma, adding a personalized mRNA therapy to pembrolizumab raised two-year recurrence-free survival from 70.0% to 82.2%. (Georgina V. Long Muhammad A. Khattak Helen J. Gogas Dirk Schadendorf Ana Arance Matteo S. Carlino Piotr Rutkowski Gareth Rivalland Antoni Ribas Janice M. Mehnert Patrick A. item.title: Cross-species multiomic atlas of the primate basal ganglia
item.description: A cell-by-cell atlas of 1.8 million nuclei from human, macaque and marmoset basal ganglia finds 61 cell types conserved over 76 million years and maps psychiatric and neurodegenerative risk onto specific cells. (Nelson J. Johansen, Yuanyuan Fu, Matthew Schmitz et al. · Allen Institute)

item.title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
item.description: In mice, the gut antibody IgA slows the renewal of the colon lining through a surface protein called DMBT1, and its absence raises susceptibility to colorectal tumors. (Gregory P. Donaldson, Gabriella Lima dos Reis, Marwa Saad et al. · The Rockefeller University)

item.title: Beam's base-edited sickle cell therapy keeps patients free of severe pain crises for a year in its pivotal trial
item.description: Beam Therapeutics says its one-time base-edited cell therapy, risto-cel, met its main goal of 12 months without severe pain crises in a 49-patient single-arm trial, and plans a US filing. (PharmaShots (summary of Beam's press release), BioPharm International)

item.title: A Lancet Psychiatry analysis compares how well 21 antidepressants keep depression at bay over months to years
item.description: Pooling 115 studies longer than 12 weeks, researchers found escitalopram, duloxetine and agomelatine somewhat more likely than fluoxetine to bring lasting improvement; experts call the differences modest. (The New York Times, BBC News)

item.title: Everyone in a 100,000-person All of Us sample carries gene variants that affect medicines, and a quarter got an affected drug
item.description: A Pitt-led analysis of nearly 100,000 genomes found every participant carried at least one drug-relevant variant (median nine), 24.4% had been prescribed an affected drug, and over 17,000 variants were new. (University of Pittsburgh via Medical Xpress, STAT, Science Translational Medicine)

item.title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
item.description: In lab-grown human neurons lacking the ALS protein TDP-43, fixing one splicing error in the synapse gene UNC13A with an antisense drug restored communication between neurons. (Matthew J. Keuss, Peter Harley, Eugeni Ryadnov et al. · King's College London; University College London; Francis Crick Institute; Leibniz-FMP; Trace Neuroscience)

item.title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
item.description: Yearly stored blood samples show that in two-thirds of women who later got acute myeloid leukaemia, the first driver mutation arose before age 20, and mutant clones then grew predictably. (Caroline J. Watson, Gladys Y. P. Poon, Hamish A. J. MacGregor et al. · University of Cambridge; University College London)

item.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
item.description: GPS-tracked tapirs and giant anteaters in Brazil carried more microplastics in their blood when their home ranges held more human disturbance or lay nearer waste facilities. (Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz, Arnaud L. J. Desbiez, Mario Henrique Alves et al. · University of British Columbia (Kelowna); Center for Advanced Systems Understanding (CASUS), Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf)

item.title: FDA orders a rare optic-nerve warning on all GLP-1 drugs
item.description: The FDA will require every GLP-1 medicine to carry a warning of a potential increased risk of NAION, a rare condition that can cause permanent vision loss in one eye. (FDA, CBS News)

item.title: FDA approves asundexian, the first factor XIa blocker, to prevent a second stroke
item.description: The FDA approved Bayer's once-daily pill Sunharbo (asundexian) alongside antiplatelet therapy after a mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic stroke or high-risk TIA, after a 12,327-person trial showed a 26% lower risk of ischemic stroke. (FDA, pharmaphorum)

item.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke
item.description: In 4,368 people with prior stroke or TIA, aiming for systolic blood pressure under 120 mm Hg rather than 140 cut major cardiovascular events by 21%, at the cost of more kidney-function events. item.title: Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease
item.description: Monthly ziltivekimab, an IL-6 antibody, sharply cut inflammatory markers in 6,376 people with atherosclerosis and kidney disease but did not change heart attack, stroke or cardiovascular death. item.title: A single–amino acid difference between rodent and human Andes virus affects viral glycoprotein trafficking
item.description: One amino acid differs between rodent and human Andes virus glycoproteins, and swapping it changed how long the protein stays in the Golgi and how fast virus-like particles are released in human cells. (Santiago Vidal-Freire, Natalia M. Ferressini-Gerpe, Carla M. Bellomo et al. · Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; Administración Nacional de Laboratorios e Institutos de Salud Dr. Carlos G. Malbrán (ANLIS); Centro Ciencia y Vida and Universidad San Sebastián; U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases; National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases)

item.title: Lp(a)-lowering drug pelacarsen cuts the target by 78% but not heart attacks or strokes, in a large phase 3 trial
item.description: In Lp(a)HORIZON, pelacarsen lowered lipoprotein(a) by about 78% in over 8,300 people with heart disease, yet heart attacks, strokes and cardiovascular deaths occurred at the same rate as on placebo. (American Heart Association, Healio, American College of Cardiology)

item.title: Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease
item.description: In a randomized trial of about 1,880 adults over 70 without heart disease, stopping statins was statistically noninferior over two years, but cardiovascular events were more frequent over longer follow-up. item.title: Noise pollution alters the body or behavior of 80% of animal species studied, a Science analysis finds
item.description: A pooled analysis of 214 experiments on 177 species found human-made noise changed physiology or behavior in eight of ten species and cut animal numbers by about 37% in noisy areas. (Phys.org, Science (study DOI))

item.title: Parkinson's may be driven by a vicious cycle that clogs the brain's waste drainage
item.description: Misfolded alpha-synuclein appears to inflame the lymphatic vessels that drain the brain, which then clear it less well, in human tissue and mice. (New Scientist, Journal of Experimental Medicine (study))

item.title: FDA grants accelerated approval to a subcutaneous antibody for previously treated head and neck cancer
item.description: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma after chemotherapy and immunotherapy, based on a 42% response rate in 102 patients. (FDA, Johnson & Johnson (OrigAMI-4 results release))

item.title: A hair and 1,000 seeds from a Siberian tomb give the oldest directly dated evidence of cannabis intoxication
item.description: Archaeologists found about 1,000 cannabis seeds and hair carrying a breakdown product of THC in a Scythian princely tomb in Siberia, dated to the early eighth century B.C., in a study in Science. (University of Bern, New Scientist, Scientific American)

item.title: British health worker with Ebola flown home as the Congo outbreak passes 10,000 cases
item.description: A British healthcare worker infected in DR Congo is being evacuated to the UK, the first British case of an outbreak that has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and has no approved treatment. (The Guardian, ECDC)

item.title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
item.description: Researchers built the largest map yet of how essential genes interact in the tuberculosis bacterium, finding nearly 6,500 interactions that could guide new drug targets and antibiotic combinations. (Isaac J. Kresse, Natalie Y. Sayegh, Vanisha Munsamy-Govender et al. · Rockefeller University)

item.title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
item.description: A global analysis of 45 threats to more than 21,000 freshwater species finds farming, dams and agricultural runoff dominate, and that freshwater species face higher threat on average than land species. (Christophe Brabant, Laura Pollock, Jonas Geldmann et al. · McGill University)

item.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
item.description: A large international randomized trial found no evidence that prone positioning or high-frequency oscillatory ventilation improves ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome. (Martha A Q Curley, Martin C J Kneyber, Ira M Cheifetz et al.)

item.title: First measles death in New York State in 30 years
item.description: A child in Lewis County, New York, died of measles, the state's first measles death in 30 years, as US cases reach their highest level in about 35 years. (The Guardian, CIDRAP, Gothamist, WRGB (CBS6 Albany))

item.title: FDA finalizes potency guidance for cell and gene therapies
item.description: The FDA issued final guidance telling makers of cell and gene therapies to build a plan proving that every batch is potent before it reaches a patient. (FDA)

item.title: English A&Es to use early warning scores for sick children
item.description: NHS England is introducing a vital-signs scoring system for children in emergency departments this winter, with parents' concerns able to trigger urgent review regardless of score. (The Guardian, BBC News)

item.title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
item.description: In a randomized trial of 744 older adults with moderate aortic stenosis and risk features, early valve replacement cut two-year death or heart failure events from 23.9% to 16.7%.
